doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Balancing NYU teaching with touring
summary: She directs NYU's percussion program part time; the school is flexible, she took one semester off for a tour, and subs are easy to find.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: You seem to be one of the few people I’ve met who manages to balance a good deal of performing with your educational obligations. Would you say that’s true?

Yeah. Sometimes it’s a struggle to balance it and that’s probably the most major difficulty that I have. I’m lucky to be at a school, right at New York University, well part time there first of all, even though I direct the entire percussion program. And also the school seems to be flexible with their performing arts faculty. They see merit in us going around the world and mentioning where I work. And that’s what attracts some students. But it’s true, it’s always a dilemma, like if one of my bands is going on the road for ten weeks and I have to hope that I can get out of my job.
What to do with the students. Do you have subs you call in? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Yeah. I’ve only taken off actually one full semester from school when my band had, I think we had a twelve week tour. I said to my boss I’ve been here for ten years, I need to get out for a semester. And he let me go, which is nice.

Yeah. I don’t know if that’s common for part time people. But anyway he let me out so that was good. Other times it’s a lot of well-qualified subs, which are easy to find in New York. There’s a lot of good players, teachers.
